name: app-screens-row
title: App screens row
description: A row of CSS-drawn phone frames with a caption under each, the middle one larger, scrolling sideways with snap on a phone.
docs: Pass title, description and screens (four to six, each with a src, alt text, a caption, the image's width and height, and optionally a srcSet, sizes, a blurDataUrl and priority). Every screen is a figure with a caption, in a phone drawn in CSS that follows both themes and costs no bytes; the screenshots are shown on a 9:19.5 screen, so crop them to that. On a section 896px wide or more the row is a grid in which the featured screen (the middle one, or featuredIndex) is larger and the others stand on the same line, a little lower, with their captions level; below that it is a sideways scroller that snaps to a screen and lets the next one peek in. The scroller is a region named App screens that the keyboard can reach and scroll with the arrow keys, Home and End, and it is a stop in the tab order only while there is something to scroll. With a mouse it shows a thin scrollbar to drag, and on touch the scrollbar is hidden. Give each row its own labels.region when a page has more than one. Pass bleed (your page's side padding) and the scroller runs to the edge of the screen on a phone. Pictures keep their proportions before they load, show a blurred seed from blurDataUrl until they arrive and are lazy unless priority is set; renderImage plugs in next/image. Only the scroll region is a client component.
